findings.title: Timing Leak in Email Comparison
findings.description: The length check before timingSafeEqual still leaks timing information about credential lengths. Attackers can determine the length of the admin email through timing analysis.
findings.code: if (emailBuffer.length === adminEmailBuffer.length) { try { emailMatch = timingSafeEqual(emailBuffer, adminEmailBuffer) } ... }
findings.recommendation: Always run comparison with buffer of same length to prevent length-based timing attacks

findings.title: IP Spoofing Risk in Rate Limiter (Configuration Dependent)
findings.description: The x-forwarded-for header is trusted without validation. This is only safe if running behind a trusted reverse proxy. In a properly configured production environment with a load balancer, this is the standard and correct pattern.
findings.recommendation: Add documentation explaining the requirement for a trusted proxy. This is a standard pattern in production.
findings.impact: Prevents confusion about proxy requirements. No actual vulnerability if behind trusted proxy.
findings.note: This is the correct pattern for production with a trusted proxy. Add a comment documenting this requirement.
